correctness.rationale: On the two-dimensional column span the sketch difference form aaᵀ−bbᵀ has trace δ and determinant −h. Its positive and negative eigendirections give independent χ²_s variables by Gaussian rotation, and the negative difference event is a symmetric beta lower tail at the stated x. Schur complements give the two projection losses h/α and h/β and the optimal loss h/Λ. At fixed unequal column norms, x increases strictly as the absolute correlation decreases, giving the sharp orthogonal maximum and collinear infimum. On [0,1/2] the beta tail decreases with s: folding about 1/2 gives a density ratio decreasing in distance from the center for larger s, hence a smaller folded upper tail. Thus p_s≤x≤β/(α+β) for s≥2, yielding E_s≤2h/(α+β)<2h/Λ on full-rank inputs. The equal-norm near-parallel family has ratio 1+cos θ irrespective of the pivot; the orthogonal family with small squared norm t has one-row error ratio 1+(t⁻¹−1)(2/π)arctan√t, which diverges. Integrating the endpoint beta density gives the additional fixed-s anisotropy law. Recorded code corroborates the finite cases and laws; no simulation is needed for the theorem.
residual_risks: No finite-precision, multi-column, or repeated-pivot conclusion follows. The factor is for expected squared Frobenius error, not a probability bound.

evidence: The known orthogonal family already shows the limiting factor 2 for two rows; its excess instead vanishes at higher widths.
The equal-norm, nearly parallel family reaches supremum 2 at every width, irrespective of selection; the uniform upper bound needs control of correlated norm tails and the Gram residual ratio.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The combined general upper bound, all-width sharpness and correlated probability law are not special cases of the inspected prior results. Distinction is not claimed for the constituent diagonal or two-row probability evaluations.

evidence: The golden-ratio orientation record gives p₂=(1−δ/√(δ²+4L))/2 at proof offset 3849. Identifying L with the Gram determinant gives exactly the frozen p₂, since Δ²=δ²+4h.
The sharp randomized LU threshold record 3ec204a30cf5 uses a projected-row selection followed by entry selection and a different update loss.
Duersch–Gu p. 6 and Theorem 3.1 describe marginal norm estimates and conditional truncation after pivot selection.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The first formula genuinely supplies the probability, and with either-column projection errors also supplies the two-row expectation. The LU rule and postselection QRCP laws are not equivalent to the arbitrary-s initial correlated comparison.

evidence: The exact first-pivot/runner-up Finding at offset 1307 gives the probability under orthogonality; two columns give the symmetric beta tail at β/(α+β).

The moment-cutoff Finding and assumptions at offsets 0–3497 give exact normalized CPQR moments on diag(κ,1) for s≥2. Setting moment order to two gives the same diagonal ratio and limiting two-row factor. Its displayed beta expression extends to s=1 by the one-degree-of-freedom calculation, but s=1 is outside its stated CPQR scope.
The golden-ratio record provides the exact correlated s=2 slice.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These are exact indexed formula families, not approximations. The diagonal projection and cross approximation coincide, as do the rank-one residual spectral and Frobenius norms there. None of these exact slices is a formula for arbitrary correlated columns at every width.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the sharp worst-case expectation theorem for arbitrary real rank-two two-column inputs, with the full correlated beta law at arbitrary sketch width. Exact catalogue overlaps cover the two-row correlated pivot probability and orthogonal subfamilies, not that full conclusion. Gaussian pivoting, chi-square laws and deterministic projection identities are not themselves new.
residual_risks: The targeted primary-literature search had low signal and cannot establish exhaustive priority. Classical Gaussian quadratic-form comparisons may present other equivalent probability formulas.
Catalogue dates are not used as evidence for priority or provenance.

checked_sources: Diagonal moment-cutoff and correlated two-row comparison records
value.rationale: The minimal-width result gives an exact expectation boundary for a standard randomized pivot mechanism, not just a rephrasing of the beta distribution. The one-row failure arises from rare orthogonal mispivots; with more rows the persistent sharp factor of two instead comes from nearly collinear equal-norm columns. Distinguishing these mechanisms clarifies what oversampling can and cannot improve in this narrow setting.
residual_risks: The result addresses the two-column first pivot only; it is not a performance guarantee for a full QR routine.
